exposure: ventral hernias (epidemiologic aspects, clinical features, types)
surgical methods for ventral hernia repair (darning herniorrhaphy, mesh repair, open on lay repairs, elective vs. emergency repair)
risk factors for incisional hernias (laparotomy, gynaecological surgeries, hysterectomy, caesarean section, midline incisions)
outcome: incidence of ventral hernias (incisional, umbilical, epigastric)
prevalence of ventral hernias by age and sex
presentation of ventral hernias (painless swelling, pain, irreducibility, obstruction)
complications following ventral hernia repairs (pain, fever, seroma formation, wound dehiscence, pelvic collection)
cohort: 200 patients with ventral hernias, predominantly aged 40-60 years, with a mean age of 46.14 years.
finding: Ventral hernias were found to be more prevalent in elderly and female patients, with incisional, umbilical, and epigastric types being most common, and laparotomy, gynaecological procedures, and midline incisions identified as major risk factors for incisional hernias.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was identified as a gynaecological surgery that could lead to the development of incisional hernias.
